text:
jordan_ops: FYI we have a high-severity ticket from Acme (Dedicated, na-west2). Multiple 429s + 503s during placements and sustained tail latency for token generation. Customer says failover to eu-west1 didn’t happen for some of their routed traffic.

sara_support: Can you paste the top-level error logs? I pulled the support case - they're on reserved pool R-PROD-9. Customer reports spike at 10:18 PST.

jordan_ops: Ops alert + excerpt:

ops-bot: ALERT: placement_failures high on na-west2-dedicated (rpool=R-PROD-9) 10:17-10:27

jordan_ops: ```
ERROR placement: allocation failed: no compatible node found
req_id=abc123 model=gpt-neox-seq len=1024 pool=R-PROD-9
cause=insufficient_gpus region=na-west2
```

liam_infra: Looks like the scheduler tried to scale but hit AZ quota. I see repeated autoscale attempts:

```
autoscaler: attempt=1 -> launch instance g4dn.xlarge (quota check: failed)
autoscaler: attempt=2 -> launch instance g4dn.xlarge (quota check: failed)
```

miguel_se: Customer traces show router attempted region-failover but the policy requires a cold-retry window 30s before cross-region fallback. They had bursts <30s so many requests retried locally and hit throttles.

elaine_custsuccess: They also flagged a billing hold that was applied yesterday morning to a different account. Not sure if that affected their reserved capacity entitlement. @sara_support can you confirm?

sara_support: Confirmed: billing hold was for a separate tenant; R-PROD-9 should be unaffected. I've attached case note: "billing: hold cleared for tenant-id 7654 on 2245120000".

liam_infra: Repro steps I'm running:
1) Use reserved-pool token for R-PROD-9
2) Fire concurrent placement requests (100 req/s) with model=gpt-neox-seq and seq_len=1024
3) Observe scheduler logs + 429s

cURL repro:```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/infer \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN_RPROD9}" \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-neox-seq","input":"x"*1024}' -H "Content-Type: application/json" -s -D -\
```

miguel_se: When I replayed with the same header + token while forcing region=eu-west1 the requests succeeded. So it's capacity constrained in na-west2.

jordan_ops: Do we have noisy-tenant suspects on that pool? Any eviction logs?

liam_infra: There are a few noisy tenants on the same dedicated cluster: tenant=video-renderer-1 had long-running infer jobs and was ramping up at 10:10. Eviction traces show preemption not allowed because pool is configured as reserved. So customer isolation is only logical; heavy concurrent usage still crowds scheduling.

ops-bot: NOTE: Current cluster utilization na-west2-dedicated: 94% GPUs in use, pending queue=72, fail_rate=12% over last 10m.

sara_support: Customer wants immediate mitigation and an explanation how this escaped the SLA guardrails. Propose options: 1) manual capacity bleed from spare pools 2) immediate cross-region routing override for R-PROD-9 3) credit + postmortem. Thoughts?

liam_infra: Short-term: I can trigger a manual routing override to route R-PROD-9 to eu-west1 for 10m, but that will add cross-region egress and latency. Need approvals from eng-sre.

miguel_se: Long-term: we need stricter autoscaler quota checks earlier (fail fast), and maybe a fast-fallback logic that ignores the 30s cold-window when placement failure rate > X. Also improve noisy-tenant detection to throttle heavy tail jobs even in reserved pools.

elaine_custsuccess: I'll propose credits for affected window and schedule a customer call after we confirm fix.

jordan_ops: Action items:
- @liam_infra trigger manual routing override -> in progress
- @sara_support confirm billing/credits -> assigned
- @miguel_se file follow-up feature request: fast cross-region fallback + noisy-tenant throttling
- Ops: collect scheduler traces for 10:00-10:30 and upload to incident ticket.

sara_support: Update: override applied at 10:33, customer reports immediate drop in errors, but higher latency (median +120ms). They accepted temporary routing. Will keep monitoring. :thumbsup:

liam_infra: Uploaded traces to the ticket: link: https://redwood.internal/incident/2245123456/traces (internal)

jordan_ops: OK closing the active page when monitoring looks stable. We still need to author the postmortem and customer-facing RCA.

elaine_custsuccess: Scheduling RCA meeting for 2245124200.

sara_support: Thanks all. I'll update the case notes and send the initial customer-facing statement.
